sw.R: Kisha ulishuka hadi chini ya kilima kinachotazama Bonde la Hinomu, upande wa kaskazini wa Bonde la Refaimu. Ulishuka Bonde la Hinomu, kando ya mteremko ulio kusini mwa mji wa Wayebusi. Kisha ukashuka hadi chemchemi ya En-rogeli.

es.L: Y baja la frontera al extremo del monte que [está] frente al valle de Ben-hinom, que [está] en el valle de Refaim al norte; y baja por el valle de Hinom a la ladera del jebuseo por el sur, y baja a En-rogel.
es.B: Luego la frontera baja al pie del monte que está frente al valle de Ben-hinom, en el extremo norte del valle de Refaim. Baja por el valle de Hinom, por la ladera sur de la ciudad jebusea, y sigue hasta En-rogel.
es.R: Después bajaba al pie del monte que mira al valle de Hinom, en el extremo norte del valle de Refaim. Bajaba por el valle de Hinom, por la ladera al sur de la ciudad de los jebuseos. Luego bajaba hasta el manantial de En-rogel.

fr.L: Et la frontière descend vers l’extrémité de la montagne qui [est] en face de la vallée de Ben-Hinnom, qui [est] dans la vallée des Rephaïm au nord ; et elle descend la vallée de Hinnom vers le flanc du Jébusien au sud, et descend vers En-Roguel.
fr.B: Puis la frontière descend au pied de la colline qui fait face à la vallée de Ben-Hinnom, à l’extrémité nord de la vallée des Rephaïm. Elle descend la vallée de Hinnom, le long du versant sud de la ville jébusienne, et descend jusqu’à En-Roguel.
fr.R: Ensuite, elle descendait jusqu’au pied de la colline qui domine la vallée de Hinnom, à l’extrémité nord de la vallée des Rephaïm. Elle descendait la vallée de Hinnom, le long de la colline au sud de la ville des Jébusiens. Puis elle descendait jusqu’à la source d’En-Roguel.

vi.L: Ranh giới đi xuống chân ngọn đồi đối diện thung lũng Bên-Hi-nôm, [ở] trong thung lũng Rê-pha-im về phía bắc; và nó đi xuống thung lũng Hi-nôm đến sườn [đất] người Giê-bu-sít ở phía nam, rồi đi xuống Ên-Rô-ghên.
vi.B: Rồi ranh giới đi xuống chân ngọn đồi đối diện thung lũng Bên-Hi-nôm, ở đầu phía bắc thung lũng Rê-pha-im. Nó chạy xuống thung lũng Hi-nôm, dọc sườn phía nam của thành người Giê-bu-sít, và xuống đến Ên-Rô-ghên.
vi.R: Rồi nó đi xuống chân ngọn đồi nhìn ra thung lũng Hi-nôm, ở đầu phía bắc thung lũng Rê-pha-im. Nó đi xuống thung lũng Hi-nôm, dọc sườn đồi phía nam thành của người Giê-bu-sít. Rồi nó đi xuống suối Ên-Rô-ghên.

ko.L: 그리고 경계는 북쪽으로 르바임 골짜기에 있는, 벤힌놈 골짜기 맞은편 산의 끝으로 내려가고, 힌놈 골짜기로 남쪽 여부스 비탈로 내려가서, 엔로겔로 내려간다.
ko.B: 그다음에 경계는 르바임 골짜기 북쪽 끝에 있는, 벤힌놈 골짜기를 마주한 언덕 기슭으로 내려간다. 거기에서 힌놈 골짜기를 따라 여부스 성읍의 남쪽 비탈로 내려가서 엔로겔에 이른다.
ko.R: 그다음에 경계는 르바임 골짜기 북쪽 끝에 있는, 힌놈 골짜기가 내려다보이는 언덕 기슭으로 내려갔다. 그리고 힌놈 골짜기를 따라 여부스 사람들의 성읍 남쪽 산비탈로 내려갔다. 그다음에 엔로겔 샘으로 내려갔다.

pt.L: E a fronteira desce até a extremidade do monte que [está] em frente do vale de Ben-Hinom, que [está] no vale de Refaim, ao norte; e desce o vale de Hinom até a encosta do jebuseu, ao sul, e desce a En-Rogel.
pt.B: Depois a fronteira desce até o pé do monte que fica em frente do vale de Ben-Hinom, na extremidade norte do vale de Refaim. Ela desce pelo vale de Hinom, ao longo da encosta sul da cidade dos jebuseus, até En-Rogel.
pt.R: Depois ela descia até o pé do monte que fica de frente para o vale de Hinom, na ponta norte do vale de Refaim. Ela descia pelo vale de Hinom, ao longo da encosta ao sul da cidade dos jebuseus. Depois descia até a fonte de En-Rogel.

decisions.choice: the valley of Ben-hinnom, the valley of Hinnom: the valley south and west of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The name means "valley of the son of Hinnom", called the valley of Hinnom later in the verse. It curves around the south-west of Jerusalem. In later times children were burned there in worship of other gods (2 Kings 23:10; Jeremiah 7:31), and its name became a word for the place of final judgment.

decisions.choice: the valley of Rephaim: a broad valley south-west of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Its name recalls the Rephaim, a people of great size remembered from early times (Deuteronomy 2:11). David later fought the Philistines there (2 Samuel 5:18-22).

decisions.choice: the slope of the Jebusite: the ridge of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: "The Jebusite" stands for the Jebusites' town, Jebus, that is Jerusalem (15:8; verse 28). The border runs along the south of the city, so Jerusalem falls inside Benjamin's land, though the Jebusites were not yet driven out (15:63; Judges 1:21).

decisions.choice: En-rogel: a spring below Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The name means "spring of the fuller" or "of the foot". It lay where the valley of Hinnom meets the Kidron valley, south-east of the city (2 Samuel 17:17; 1 Kings 1:9).

decisions.choice: the Jebusite city / the city of the Jebusites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "city" so it is clear that a place is meant, not a person (m3).

decisions.choice: the spring of En-rogel
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the spring" so young readers know what En-rogel is (m4).

decisions.choice: o vale de Ben-Hinom, o vale de Hinom; o vale de Refaim; En-Rogel
decisions.reason: "Vale" stays lowercase before the name, as in "o vale de Acor" (7:26). The names take their Brazilian forms; "En-" (spring) keeps its Hebrew shape in a name, and Readable adds "a fonte de", as the English Readable does (r-en-2). "A cidade dos jebuseus" (B, R) says that a place is meant (m3).

source.text: וְתָאַ֣ר מִצָּפ֗וֹן וְיָצָא֙ עֵ֣ין שֶׁ֔מֶשׁ וְיָצָא֙ אֶל־גְּלִיל֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־נֹ֖כַח מַעֲלֵ֣ה אֲדֻמִּ֑ים וְיָרַ֕ד אֶ֥בֶן בֹּ֖הַן בֶּן־רְאוּבֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And is drawn from [the] north and goes out [to] En-shemesh, and goes out to Geliloth, which [is] opposite [the] ascent of Adummim, and goes down [to the] stone of Bohan [the] son of Reuben.

en.L: And it is drawn from the north and goes out to En-shemesh, and goes out to Geliloth, which [is] opposite the ascent of Adummim, and goes down to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben.
en.B: From there it bends northward and goes out to En-shemesh, then on to Geliloth, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim, and goes down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
en.R: Then the border turned north and went out to En-shemesh. It went on to Geliloth, across from the road that climbs up to Adummim. Then it went down to the Stone of Bohan, who was a son of Reuben.

sw.L: Na unazunguka kutoka kaskazini na kutokea En-shemeshi, na kutokea Gelilothi, ulio mkabala na mwinuko wa Adumimu, na kushuka hadi jiwe la Bohani mwana wa Reubeni.
sw.B: Kutoka hapo unapinda kuelekea kaskazini, unatokea En-shemeshi, kisha Gelilothi, ulio mkabala na Mwinuko wa Adumimu, na kushuka hadi Jiwe la Bohani mwana wa Reubeni.
sw.R: Kisha mpaka uligeuka kaskazini ukaenda hadi En-shemeshi. Ukaendelea hadi Gelilothi, mkabala na njia inayopanda kwenda Adumimu. Kisha ukashuka hadi Jiwe la Bohani, aliyekuwa mwana wa Reubeni.

es.L: Y se traza desde el norte, y sale a En-semes, y sale a Gelilot, que [está] frente a la subida de Adumín, y baja a la piedra de Bohán hijo de Rubén.
es.B: De allí se curva hacia el norte y sale a En-semes, luego a Gelilot, que está frente a la subida de Adumín, y baja a la Piedra de Bohán hijo de Rubén.
es.R: Luego la frontera giraba al norte y salía a En-semes. Seguía hasta Gelilot, frente al camino que sube a Adumín. Después bajaba a la Piedra de Bohán, que era hijo de Rubén.

fr.L: Et elle s’infléchit depuis le nord, et sort vers En-Shémesh, et sort vers Gueliloth, qui [est] en face de la montée d’Adoummim, et descend vers la pierre de Bohan, fils de Ruben.
fr.B: De là, elle s’incurve vers le nord et sort vers En-Shémesh, puis vers Gueliloth, en face de la montée d’Adoummim, et descend jusqu’à la Pierre de Bohan, fils de Ruben.
fr.R: Puis la frontière tournait vers le nord et allait jusqu’à En-Shémesh. Elle continuait jusqu’à Gueliloth, en face de la route qui monte vers Adoummim. Ensuite, elle descendait jusqu’à la Pierre de Bohan, qui était un fils de Ruben.

vi.L: Nó kéo từ phía bắc và đi ra Ên-Sê-mết, đi ra Ghê-li-lốt, [nơi] đối diện dốc A-đu-mim, rồi đi xuống hòn đá của Bô-han con trai Ru-bên.
vi.B: Từ đó nó uốn về phía bắc, ra đến Ên-Sê-mết, rồi tiếp đến Ghê-li-lốt, đối diện dốc A-đu-mim, và đi xuống Đá Bô-han con trai Ru-bên.
vi.R: Rồi ranh giới quay về phía bắc và ra đến Ên-Sê-mết. Nó đi tiếp đến Ghê-li-lốt, đối diện con đường dốc lên A-đu-mim. Rồi nó đi xuống Đá Bô-han. Bô-han là một con trai của Ru-bên.

ko.L: 그리고 그것은 북쪽에서 이어져 엔세메스로 나가고, 아둠밈 비탈 맞은편에 있는 글릴롯으로 나가서, 르우벤의 아들 보한의 돌로 내려간다.
ko.B: 거기에서 북쪽으로 굽어 돌아 엔세메스로 나가고, 아둠밈 고개 맞은편에 있는 글릴롯으로 나가서, 르우벤의 아들 보한의 돌로 내려간다.
ko.R: 그다음에 경계는 북쪽으로 돌아 엔세메스로 나갔다. 그리고 아둠밈으로 올라가는 길 건너편의 글릴롯까지 갔다. 그다음에 보한의 돌로 내려갔는데, 보한은 르우벤의 아들이었다.

pt.L: E se estende desde o norte, e sai a En-Semes, e sai para Gelilote, que [está] em frente da subida de Adumim, e desce à pedra de Boã, filho de Rúben.
pt.B: Dali ela faz uma curva para o norte e sai em En-Semes, segue até Gelilote, que fica em frente da Subida de Adumim, e desce até a Pedra de Boã, filho de Rúben.
pt.R: Então a fronteira virava para o norte e ia até En-Semes. Seguia até Gelilote, do outro lado do caminho que sobe para Adumim. Depois descia até a Pedra de Boã. Boã era filho de Rúben.

decisions.choice: is drawn from the north: bends to the north
decisions.reason: The verb is the one in verse 14. "From the north" here means the line curves round to run along a northern course, as the border turns away from Jerusalem toward the east.

decisions.choice: En-shemesh and Geliloth: places on the road from Jerusalem to Jericho
decisions.reason: En-shemesh means "spring of the sun"; it is often placed at the spring east of Bethany. Geliloth means "circles" or "districts". Judah's border at this point names Gilgal (15:7), "circle" of stones, which is probably the same place by a related name, not the Gilgal near Jericho.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Adummim: the climb up from the Jordan valley toward Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Adummim means "red places", perhaps from the reddish rock. The road climbs steeply here (15:7).

decisions.choice: the stone of Bohan son of Reuben: a known landmark
decisions.reason: The same stone marks Judah's border (15:6). Nothing more is known of it or of Bohan, a man of the tribe of Reuben, after whom it was named.

decisions.choice: the road that climbs up to Adummim
decisions.reason: Readable says what the "ascent" is, a road climbing a steep slope (m3).

decisions.choice: En-Semes, Gelilote; a subida de Adumim (L), a Subida de Adumim (B), o caminho que sobe para Adumim (R); a pedra (L), a Pedra (B, R) de Boã
decisions.reason: As Numbers 34:4 has "a subida de Acrabim" (L) and "a Subida de Acrabim" (B) in Portuguese, the climbing road (m3) is "subida", capitalised as a name at Balanced; Readable says what it is, as the English Readable does. The stone is a known landmark (m4), so Balanced and Readable capitalise it as a name.

source.text: וְעָבַ֛ר אֶל־כֶּ֥תֶף מוּל־הָֽעֲרָבָ֖ה צָפ֑וֹנָה וְיָרַ֖ד הָעֲרָבָֽתָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And passes on to [the] slope opposite the Arabah northward and goes down to the Arabah.

en.L: And it passes on to the slope opposite the Arabah on the north, and goes down to the Arabah.
en.B: It passes on to the northern slope opposite the Arabah and goes down into the Arabah.
en.R: It went on along the hillside north of the Arabah, the Jordan Valley. Then it went down into the valley.

sw.L: Na unapita hadi mteremko ulio mkabala na Araba upande wa kaskazini, na kushuka hadi Araba.
sw.B: Unapita hadi mteremko wa kaskazini unaoelekeana na Araba, na kushuka kuingia Araba.
sw.R: Ulipita kando ya mteremko ulio kaskazini mwa Araba, yaani Bonde la Yordani. Kisha ukashuka kuingia bondeni.

es.L: Y pasa a la ladera frente al Arabá por el norte, y baja al Arabá.
es.B: Pasa por la ladera norte frente al Arabá y baja al Arabá.
es.R: Seguía por la ladera al norte del Arabá, el valle del Jordán. Luego bajaba al valle.

fr.L: Et elle passe vers le flanc en face de l’Araba, au nord, et descend vers l’Araba.
fr.B: Elle passe vers le versant nord, en face de l’Araba, et descend dans l’Araba.
fr.R: Elle longeait la colline au nord de l’Araba, la vallée du Jourdain. Puis elle descendait dans la vallée.

vi.L: Nó đi qua sườn đối diện A-ra-ba ở phía bắc, và đi xuống A-ra-ba.
vi.B: Nó đi qua sườn phía bắc đối diện A-ra-ba, rồi đi xuống A-ra-ba.
vi.R: Nó chạy dọc sườn đồi phía bắc A-ra-ba, tức là thung lũng sông Giô-đanh. Rồi nó đi xuống thung lũng.

ko.L: 그리고 그것은 북쪽으로 아라바 맞은편 비탈로 지나가서 아라바로 내려간다.
ko.B: 경계는 아라바 맞은편의 북쪽 비탈로 지나서 아라바로 내려간다.
ko.R: 경계는 요단 골짜기인 아라바 북쪽의 산비탈을 따라갔다. 그리고 그 골짜기로 내려갔다.

pt.L: E passa à encosta em frente da Arabá, ao norte, e desce à Arabá.
pt.B: Ela passa pela encosta norte, em frente da Arabá, e desce até a Arabá.
pt.R: Ela seguia pela encosta ao norte da Arabá, o vale do Jordão. Depois descia até o vale.

decisions.choice: opposite the Arabah: the Hebrew text as it stands
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "to the slope opposite the Arabah". The ancient Greek translation reads "to the slope of Beth-arabah", a town named in verse 22 and on Judah's border (15:6). Either way the border runs along the slopes above the Jordan valley before going down into it.

decisions.choice: the Arabah: the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep rift valley that runs from the Sea of Galilee through the Dead Sea and on south (Deuteronomy 1:1; 3:17). Here it is the dry plain of the Jordan near Jericho.

decisions.choice: the Arabah, the Jordan Valley
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name the first time it comes (m2).

source.text: וְעָבַ֨ר הַגְּב֜וּל אֶל־כֶּ֣תֶף בֵּית־חָגְלָה֮ צָפוֹנָה֒ וְהָי֣וּ׀תֹּצְא֣וֹת הַגְּב֗וּל אֶל־לְשׁ֤וֹן יָם־הַמֶּ֨לַח֙ צָפ֔וֹנָה אֶל־קְצֵ֥ה הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן נֶ֑גְבָּה זֶ֖ה גְּב֥וּל נֶֽגֶב׃

records.literal_gloss: And passes on the border to [the] slope of Beth-hoglah northward, and are [the] goings out of the border at [the] tongue of [the] Sea of the Salt northward, at [the] end of the Jordan southward. This [is the] border [of the] south.

en.L: And the border passes on to the slope of Beth-hoglah on the north, and the end of the border is at the northern tongue of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This [is] the southern border.
en.B: The border passes on to the northern slope of Beth-hoglah and ends at the northern bay of the Dead Sea, where the Jordan flows into it at the south. This is the southern border.
en.R: Then the border went along the hillside north of Beth-hoglah. It ended at the north shore of the Dead Sea, where the Jordan River flows into it. That was the southern border.

sw.L: Na mpaka unapita hadi mteremko wa Beth-hogla upande wa kaskazini, na mwisho wa mpaka ni ulimi wa kaskazini wa Bahari ya Chumvi, mwisho wa kusini wa Yordani. Huu [ndio] mpaka wa kusini.
sw.B: Mpaka unapita hadi mteremko wa kaskazini wa Beth-hogla, na kuishia kwenye ghuba ya kaskazini ya Bahari ya Chumvi, mahali Yordani inapoingia baharini upande wa kusini. Huo ndio mpaka wa kusini.
sw.R: Kisha mpaka ulipita kando ya mteremko ulio kaskazini mwa Beth-hogla. Uliishia kwenye ufuo wa kaskazini wa Bahari Mfu, pale Mto Yordani unapoingia ndani yake. Huo ndio uliokuwa mpaka wa kusini.

es.L: Y pasa la frontera a la ladera de Bet-hogla por el norte, y las salidas de la frontera están en la lengua norte del mar Salado, en el extremo sur del Jordán. Esta [es] la frontera del sur.
es.B: La frontera pasa por la ladera norte de Bet-hogla y termina en la bahía norte del mar Muerto, donde el Jordán desemboca por el sur. Esta es la frontera sur.
es.R: Luego la frontera iba por la ladera al norte de Bet-hogla. Terminaba en la orilla norte del mar Muerto, donde desemboca el río Jordán. Esa era la frontera sur.

fr.L: Et la frontière passe vers le flanc de Beth-Hogla au nord, et les issues de la frontière sont à la langue de la mer Salée au nord, à l’extrémité du Jourdain au sud. Ceci [est] la frontière du sud.
fr.B: La frontière passe vers le versant nord de Beth-Hogla et aboutit à la baie nord de la mer Morte, là où le Jourdain s’y jette, au sud. Telle est la frontière sud.
fr.R: Ensuite, la frontière longeait la colline au nord de Beth-Hogla. Elle se terminait au bord nord de la mer Morte, là où le Jourdain s’y jette. C’était la frontière sud.

vi.L: Ranh giới đi qua sườn Bết-Hốt-la ở phía bắc, và cuối ranh giới là ở lưỡi phía bắc của Biển Muối, ở đầu phía nam sông Giô-đanh. Đây [là] ranh giới phía nam.
vi.B: Ranh giới đi qua sườn phía bắc Bết-Hốt-la và dừng lại ở vịnh phía bắc Biển Chết, nơi sông Giô-đanh đổ vào biển ở phía nam. Đó là ranh giới phía nam.
vi.R: Rồi ranh giới chạy dọc sườn đồi phía bắc Bết-Hốt-la. Nó dừng lại ở bờ phía bắc Biển Chết, nơi sông Giô-đanh đổ vào biển. Đó là ranh giới phía nam.

ko.L: 그리고 경계는 북쪽으로 벧호글라 비탈로 지나가고, 경계의 끝은 요단 남쪽 끝에 있는 염해의 북쪽 혀이다. 이것이 남쪽 경계이다.
ko.B: 경계는 벧호글라 북쪽 비탈로 지나서, 요단강이 남쪽으로 흘러드는 사해의 북쪽 만에서 끝난다. 이것이 남쪽 경계이다.
ko.R: 그다음에 경계는 벧호글라 북쪽의 산비탈을 따라갔다. 그리고 요단강이 흘러드는 사해의 북쪽 바닷가에서 끝났다. 그것이 남쪽 경계였다.

pt.L: E a fronteira passa à encosta de Bete-Hogla, ao norte, e o extremo da fronteira é na língua do mar Salgado, ao norte, na extremidade do Jordão, ao sul. Esta [é] a fronteira sul.
pt.B: A fronteira passa pela encosta norte de Bete-Hogla e termina na baía do norte do mar Morto, na extremidade sul do Jordão, onde ele deságua no mar. Esta é a fronteira sul.
pt.R: Depois a fronteira passava pela encosta ao norte de Bete-Hogla. Ela terminava na margem norte do mar Morto, onde o rio Jordão deságua. Essa era a fronteira sul.

decisions.choice: Beth-hoglah: a town near the north end of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Beth-hoglah lay in the plain between Jericho and the Dead Sea, on the line between Judah and Benjamin (15:6). It is counted among Benjamin's towns (verse 21).

decisions.choice: the tongue of the Salt Sea: the northern bay of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: "Tongue" is used for a bay or inlet of the sea, as at 15:2, 5. The border meets the sea at its northern tip, where the Jordan flows in.

decisions.choice: they are the goings out of the border: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) read "it is its goings out"; the reading the scribes marked (qere), followed here, is "they are the goings out of the border". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: the end of the Jordan southward: where the river ends in the sea
decisions.reason: "Southward" here goes with the end of the Jordan: its southern end, where it flows into the Dead Sea. The border that started on the slopes west of Kiriath-jearim (verse 15) ends here.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern name for the Salt Sea, as in Numbers 34:3; Literal keeps "Salt Sea" and "tongue".

decisions.choice: the cities: two lists, east and west
decisions.reason: The towns are listed in two groups, each with its own total: twelve in the east, around Jericho and Bethel (verses 21-24), and fourteen in the west, around Gibeon and Jerusalem (verses 25-28). The sentence runs on from verse 21 to the total in verse 24.

decisions.choice: Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz: towns of the Jordan plain
decisions.reason: Jericho had been destroyed and put under a curse (6:24-26), but its site is counted in Benjamin's land; it was rebuilt much later (1 Kings 16:34). Beth-hoglah is on the southern border (verse 19). Emek-keziz, "valley of Keziz", is named only here, and its site is not known.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: Balanced and Readable use "towns" for places of every size. Literal keeps "cities". The list runs on into the next verses, so every level ends this verse with a comma.

decisions.choice: the Avvim, the Parah: names with "the"
decisions.reason: Several names in these lists carry "the" (here, and Ophni, Ramah, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah and Haeleph in verses 24-28), showing that they began as ordinary words: Avvim may mean "ruins", Parah "heifer", Ramah "height", Mizpeh "lookout". The article is part of the name, not a sign of a different kind of place.

decisions.choice: Avvim, Parah, without "the"
decisions.reason: English does not put "the" before a town's name, so the article is left out at every level, here and in verses 24-28 (m1).

decisions.choice: Avvim, Parah, Ophrah: towns north-east of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Avvim is not the people called Avvites in 13:3, but a town, perhaps the same as Ai. Ophrah lay north of Michmash (1 Samuel 13:17); it is not the Ophrah of Gideon in Manasseh (Judges 6:11). Parah was probably in the valley north-east of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Kephar-ammonah: the name as written
decisions.reason: The text as written gives the name as Kephar-ammonah, "village of the Ammonite woman" or "of Ammonah". The scribes marked a reading Kephar-ammoni, "village of the Ammonites". It is the same place, which is not otherwise known.

decisions.choice: Ophni and Geba
decisions.reason: Ophni is named only here. Geba lay on a hill south of the gorge of Michmash, on the northern edge of later Judah (1 Samuel 14:5; 2 Kings 23:8); it became a town of the Levites (21:17).

decisions.choice: twelve cities and their villages: walled towns and the smaller settlements round them
decisions.reason: The word for "villages" means unwalled settlements or farmsteads. "Their" refers to the towns: each town had the open villages that belonged to it and depended on it, as throughout chapters 15 and 19.

decisions.choice: That was twelve towns, and the villages around them.
decisions.reason: Readable ends the list and gives the total as a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: doze cidades e as suas aldeias (L); doze cidades com as suas aldeias (B, R)
decisions.reason: As 13:23 sets the closing formula: the unwalled settlements that belonged to each town (m3) are "aldeias", the plain Portuguese word for a small rural settlement. With a number, Literal keeps the Hebrew "and" ("doze cidades e as suas aldeias"); Balanced and Readable say "doze cidades com as suas aldeias", the same for every numbered total in chapters 18-21, which shows that the villages went with the towns rather than being counted with them.

records.literal_gloss: and Zelah, Haeleph, and the Jebusite, that [is] Jerusalem, Gibeah, Kiriath: cities four [and] ten and their villages. This [was the] inheritance of [the] sons of Benjamin by their clans.

en.L: and Zelah, Haeleph, and the Jebusite [town], that [is] Jerusalem, Gibeah, [and] Kiriath: fourteen cities and their villages. This [was] the inheritance of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Benjamin by their clans.
en.B: Zelah, Haeleph, Jebus (that is, Jerusalem), Gibeah and Kiriath, fourteen towns and their villages. This was the inheritance of the tribe of Benjamin, clan by clan.
en.R: Zelah, Haeleph, Jebus (which is Jerusalem), Gibeah and Kiriath. In all, there were fourteen towns with their villages. This was the land that belonged to the tribe of Benjamin and its clans.

sw.L: na Sela, Haelefu, na [mji wa] Myebusi, yaani Yerusalemu, Gibea, [na] Kiriathi: miji kumi na minne na vijiji vyake. Huu [ndio] urithi wa wana wa Benyamini kufuatana na koo zao.
sw.B: Sela, Haelefu, Yebusi (yaani Yerusalemu), Gibea na Kiriathi, jumla miji kumi na minne pamoja na vijiji vyake. Huu ndio urithi wa kabila la Benyamini, ukoo kwa ukoo.
sw.R: Sela, Haelefu, Yebusi (yaani Yerusalemu), Gibea na Kiriathi. Kwa jumla ilikuwa miji kumi na minne pamoja na vijiji vyake. Hii ndiyo nchi iliyokuwa ya kabila la Benyamini na koo zake.

es.L: y Sela, Elef, y la [ciudad] jebusea, que [es] Jerusalén, Guibeá, [y] Quiriat: catorce ciudades y sus aldeas. Esta [es] la heredad de los hijos de Benjamín conforme a sus clanes.

es.R: Sela, Elef, Jebús (que es Jerusalén), Guibeá y Quiriat. En total, eran catorce pueblos con sus aldeas. Esta era la tierra que pertenecía a la tribu de Benjamín y sus clanes.

decisions.choice: the Jebusite, that is Jerusalem: the Jebusites' town
decisions.reason: "The Jebusite" names the town of the Jebusites, also called Jebus (Judges 19:10-11), which is Jerusalem. It lay on the line between Benjamin and Judah (verse 16; 15:8) and is counted here among Benjamin's towns, though the Jebusites still held it (15:63; Judges 1:21) until David took it (2 Samuel 5:6-9).

decisions.choice: Zelah, Haeleph: two towns, so that the total is fourteen
decisions.reason: The two words may be read as one name, Zelah-haeleph, but the total of fourteen needs them as two. Zelah was where Saul and Jonathan were later buried (2 Samuel 21:14). Haeleph is named only here.

decisions.choice: Gibeah, Kiriath: two towns, or one name
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "Gibeath Kiriath". As two names they make the total of fourteen. Gibeah, "the hill", was later Saul's home (1 Samuel 10:26). Kiriath, "town", may be short for Kiriath-jearim, as the ancient Greek translation reads, though that town is counted as Judah's in verse 14 and 15:60.

decisions.choice: this was the inheritance: the close of Benjamin's lot
decisions.reason: The summary repeats verse 20 and closes the account of Benjamin's land, borders and towns, before the second lot falls to Simeon (19:1).

decisions.choice: the Jebusite [town] ... [and] Kiriath
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "town" so "the Jebusite" is read as a place, and brackets "and" before the last name, which the Hebrew leaves out.

decisions.choice: Jebus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the town's name Jebus for "the Jebusite" (m1), as Judges 19:10 does.
